threads.body: [General] `getMessageId` is treated as nullable by `SqsProcessRequestAttributesGetter`, but null-valued `Attributes.of(...)` has undefined API behavior. A response with a propagated context but no message ID could therefore disrupt link extraction instead of retaining an attribute-free link. Build through `AttributesBuilder.put`, whose null handling safely omits the attribute.

replies.body:
Addressed in d3a42720fac3fd408074b2e792e57587c64ea8e9.

Analysis: Both AWS SDK message ID getters can return null, so constructing link attributes through the fixed-value factory can reject an otherwise valid propagated link. Building the attributes and passing the nullable value to AttributesBuilder.put preserves the link while omitting only the unavailable message ID.

Upsides: Receive links remain available for malformed or partial SDK responses, and both AWS SDK implementations now follow the attribute builder's documented null-omission behavior.

Downsides: Allocates a builder for each receive link instead of using the fixed-value factory; no material behavioral downside for non-null message IDs.

Correction after checking the exact OpenTelemetry API 1.65.0 implementation: the single-pair `Attributes.of` factory explicitly returns `Attributes.empty()` when `value == null`. The original direct call is therefore safe and avoids duplicating the factory's null handling, so I restored it.
